clue.text: Air likely to get the frigid 12 23 across to 21?

definitions.text: Air likely to get the frigid 12 23 across to 21?

parts.words: Air likely to get the frigid 12 23 across to 21?
parts.note: an air is a song; 12 and 23 across give PRESIDENT ELECT and 21 gives a loss of temper, so this is the aria that would anger a cold leader-in-waiting teased about the size of his hands

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which tune would make a chilly incoming leader lose his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The aria from Puccini's La Bohème is sung to a girl with cold hands; the joke is the well-worn jibe about the incoming US president's small hands, which would make him fly into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Air means a song, and this is the famous tenor aria from La Bohème, whose opening line is about a cold little hand.

clue.text: North American territory that welcomes Britain

indicators.note: welcomes means the first piece takes the second into its middle, as a host takes in a guest

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that, as in yon hill
UK, the United Kingdom, stands for Britain

explanation.surface: A North American region described as open to British arrivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' looks like a link word, but it gives YON, the archaic word for that.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the territory in north-west Canada, famous for the Klondike gold rush.

clue.text: UN article given Finnish backing without dissent

parts.note: taken as written, the United Nations
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: backing in a down clue means the word for Finnish is read in reverse, bottom to top

parts.note: Suomi is the Finnish name for Finland, so it stands for Finnish here

explanation.surface: A UN resolution gets Finland's support and passes with nobody objecting.
explanation.walkthrough: Suomi is Finland's own name for itself; turned round it gives IMOUS to end the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A unanimous decision is one that everybody agrees to, with nobody objecting.

clue.text: Ready to support Trump's leadership? Rubbish!

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits underneath, so the word for ready goes below the leading letter
leadership is the leading letter of the word for the businessman-politician

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

explanation.surface: Someone scornfully dismisses a call to stand behind Trump's leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is slang for nonsense, the scornful cry of someone hearing something worthless.

clue.text: A state of despair for Crosby, having lost his partner

definitions.meaning: a hopeless outlook, nothing left to hope for

definitions.text: for Crosby, having lost his partner
definitions.meaning: Bing Crosby made the Road films with Bob Hope; without his partner Crosby has no Bob Hope beside him

explanation.surface: Bing Crosby in despair after his comedy partner has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Bing Crosby and Bob Hope were a famous American comedy double act in the Road to ... films.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no hope is the condition of utter despair, read a second time as missing Bob Hope.

clue.text: This house could require a Mexican wall!

definitions.text: This house could require a Mexican wall!

parts.words: This house could require a Mexican wall!
parts.note: a large estate house in Mexico, which might well be surrounded by a Mexican wall, with a nod to the promised border wall

explanation.surface: A jibe at a politician's plan to build a wall on the Mexican border.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or ranch house in Mexico or another Spanish-speaking country.

clue.text: Decibel reading of jam session featuring One Direction

parts.note: N, north, is a compass direction

indicators.note: jam means to crush together, so these letters are squeezed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Measuring how loud the boy band One Direction played at a jam session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam session' reads as one musical phrase, but 'jam' is the anagram signal working on SESSION plus I and N; 'featuring' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Decibels measure loudness, so a decibel reading is a measure of how loud something is.

clue.text: 1,000 fish in organic compound

parts.note: read as one thousand: I is the Roman one and M the Roman thousand
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A thousand fish found in some organic substance.
explanation.walkthrough: '1,000' is split into one (I) and thousand (M) rather than taken as a single M.
explanation.definitionFit: An imide is a chemical compound containing a particular nitrogen group, so it is an example of an organic compound.

clue.text: Distressed about not being allowed out to eat Italian

parts.note: a. is a short form of about, in the sense of approximately

indicators.note: to eat means one word takes another inside it, as a mouth takes food

parts.note: a gated pupil is confined to school as a punishment
It is a common short form for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: Someone upset because a ban on going out stops them having an Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Gated is British school slang for being kept in as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated and distressed are synonyms for being upset and troubled.

clue.text: Dishonest, a bit like Jack?

definitions.meaning: the jack in a pack of cards is also called the knave, so this is resembling that card

explanation.surface: A slightly crooked character compared to someone named Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a rogue, so knavish behaviour is crooked and untrustworthy; the jack in cards is also the knave.

clue.text: Gaelic party no good for Lawrence, likely to get plastered

indicators.note: for means one thing is put in place of another, so the novelist's initials are swapped out

parts.note: a ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish gathering with folk music and dancing
D. H. Lawrence, the English novelist

explanation.surface: A Gaelic knees-up that's no fun for Lawrence, who might end up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' suggests drunk at a party, but it means covered in plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper surface of a room is usually covered in plaster, so it is the part likely to be plastered.

clue.text: I'm buried in part of church green

indicators.note: buried in means placed inside, as a body lies within a church

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
I'm is I am, so the letter I is what is buried

explanation.surface: Someone saying they lie buried in a corner of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or innocent, the same sense as unworldly and gullible.

clue.text: Spin doctor needs it for the boss

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the business of spin

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A political media adviser is told the boss needs it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin doctor' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'Spin' gives PR and 'doctor' rearranges NEEDS IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The president is the head of a company, country or society, so is the one in charge.

clue.text: See 1
Criticism voiced in guitarist's technique

definitions.meaning: comments given in response to someone's work
the howl an electric guitar makes when its amplified sound loops back into the pickups, used deliberately by rock players

explanation.surface: Complaints about the way a guitarist plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedback is responses and comments on a performance, and also the deliberate howl from an amplified guitar.

clue.text: Carefully chosen Demerara rum to entertain the King

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or host, so one piece holds the other inside it
rum means odd or strange, so these letters come out in a different order

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A fine Demerara rum picked out to serve to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Demerara rum is a real drink from Guyana, but 'rum' signals the anagram of DEMERARA, with K slipped inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmarked means set aside or designated for a particular purpose, so specially selected.

clue.text: Narrowly defeated Democrat in nick, having been caught!

parts.note: in cricket a nick is a thin edge off the bat
a batter who has been caught is out

explanation.surface: A Democrat locked up after being caught, beaten by a whisker.
explanation.walkthrough: D follows EDGE rather than sitting inside it. In cricket a batter who nicks the ball to a fielder is edged out, caught.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge out a rival is to beat them by a tiny margin.

clue.text: Working time involving state, typically speaking

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so the word for state goes inside

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
an age is a period of time
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Office hours spent dealing with the state, as is normal.
explanation.definitionFit: On average means as a rule or usually, the same as typically.

clue.text: To unwind, going topless, sunburn covers Demi's upper half

indicators.note: covers means one piece wraps around the other
going topless means losing the top, which in a down clue is the first letter
upper half in a down clue is the first half of the name

explanation.surface: Going topless to relax while sunburn spreads over the top of Demi Moore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' leaves UNBURN, which 'covers' wraps around the top half of Demi; Demi Moore is the American actress.
explanation.definitionFit: To unburden yourself is to unload your worries, which is a way to relax and unwind.

clue.text: Cherish sinner he converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A converted sinner who now treasures his faith.
explanation.definitionFit: To enshrine something is to hold it sacred and preserve it, so to treasure it.

clue.text: Was shot, captured by familiar killer

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: an old friend is a familiar one

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A killer is shot and caught by someone he knew.
explanation.walkthrough: Lee Harvey Oswald, who shot President Kennedy, was himself shot two days later.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee Harvey Oswald was the assassin of John F. Kennedy, so an example of a killer.

clue.text: Swing a part in Rising Damp? Oh, Deborah!

indicators.note: Rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
a part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An actress lands a part in Rising Damp, the British TV sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: Rising Damp was a 1970s British sitcom; here 'Rising' reverses the letters in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To swing, in the sense of swapping partners, is to move between beds, which is what this slang term means.

clue.text: Lose the plot, as Beowulf gets complicated

indicators.note: something that gets complicated is tangled up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The Old English poem Beowulf gets so tangled that a reader loses track of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose the plot' tempts as a literary comment, but it is the definition: to fly into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing the plot is an idiom for going mad or losing self-control, the same as flying into a rage.

clue.text: Architectural moulding for stocky cube having capacity to replace x

indicators.note: to replace means one piece is swapped in where the letter x stood

parts.note: OXO is a British brand of stock cube, a cube for making stock
taken as written
vol. is short for volume, which is capacity

explanation.surface: A mathematical riddle about a cube's capacity standing in for the unknown x.
explanation.walkthrough: OXO is a British stock cube brand.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex moulding with a quarter-round profile used in classical buildings.

clue.text: Vote in some revolting bankrupt celebrity

indicators.note: revolting says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Voting in a disgusting celebrity who has gone bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgust at the celebrity, but it signals a turn backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to choose by voting, so it means the same as to vote in.

clue.text: Leaders of European Commission lukewarm about Trump's swagger

indicators.note: leaders of means taking the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: European Commission heads unenthusiastic about Trump's boastful manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is showy brilliance or flair, close to a confident swagger.

clue.text: Fitting attempt to sneak an advantage?

definitions.meaning: a session where clothes are tried for size
an attempt to get away with something cheeky, to see what one can get

explanation.surface: A suitable bid to gain an edge on the sly.
explanation.definitionFit: A try-on is both a session trying clothes for size and a bold attempt at deception.

clue.text: Warped, sick Australian newspaperman

parts.note: crook is Australian slang for ill
ED, editor, is the person in charge of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A twisted, ailing Australian journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked means bent or twisted out of shape, the same as warped.

clue.text: Legendary climber unable to break the glass 10?

definitions.meaning: Sir Edmund ..., first with Tenzing Norgay to climb Everest
with 10 across this is the glass ceiling, the barrier to women at the top

explanation.surface: A mountaineer who could not smash a glass ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Hillary conquered Everest, and Hillary Clinton failed to become the first woman US president.

clue.text: Delaying tactics ordered by JFK?

definitions.meaning: JFK is the New York airport, whose air traffic control orders waiting planes to circle

explanation.surface: Stalling tactics demanded by President Kennedy.
explanation.walkthrough: JFK suggests the president, but here it is New York's John F. Kennedy airport.
explanation.definitionFit: A holding pattern is a waiting state where nothing advances, and also the loop aircraft fly while waiting to land.
